Where it's heading

The IEA's main forecast almost doubles data-centre electricity by 2030. Its scenarios for 2035 span 700 to 1,700 TWh, so we show all of it. The bright line is measured; the dim range hasn't happened yet.

Where the electricity goes

Of the 485 TWh the world's data centres used in 2025, AI was about 129 to 184 TWh: roughly a quarter to two-fifths. The rest runs everything else online: streaming, cloud storage, websites, email and business software.

EXPLAINED

Strain on the grid

Ireland and the eastern United States

In Ireland, data centres used 22% of all metered electricity in 2024, up from 5% in 2015. In the eastern US, a 5,250 MW increase in the PJM grid's demand forecast, almost entirely from data centres, helped drive the results of its latest capacity auction.

Sources: Central Statistics Office Ireland, 10 June 2025 · Utility Dive, 18 December 2025

Read the quotes
  • The percentage share of metered electricity consumption used by data centres rose to 22% in 2024 from 5% in 2015
    Central Statistics Office Ireland, 10 June 2025
  • In part, the latest auction results were driven by a 5,250-MW increase in PJM's demand forecast — almost entirely driven by data centers
    Utility Dive, 18 December 2025
EXPLAINED

Local air

Memphis, Tennessee

In Memphis, the county's permit lets xAI operate 15 generators at its data centre, up to 247 megawatts; TechCrunch describes them as natural gas generators. According to their manufacturer, the turbines emit nitrogen oxides, a key contributor to smog, and formaldehyde.

Sources: TechCrunch, 3 July 2025, ‘xAI gets permits for 15 natural gas generators at Memphis data center’ · NBC News, 17 June 2025

    NBC News, 17 June 2025

Prince William County, Virginia

The planned Digital Gateway would span 34 buildings and 1.7 gigawatts of data-centre capacity on 2,139 acres near Manassas National Battlefield; WTOP reported it would be the largest data-centre corridor in the world. A court found the county's advertised notice did not comply with either the state or county code.

Noise

Chandler, Arizona and Prince William County, Virginia

Residents near data centres in Prince William County say the constant drone, especially at night, causes anxiety and deprives them of sleep. Chandler, Arizona requires data centres to be built so their sound doesn't exceed the background level measured in a baseline study.

Sources: Prince William Times, 27 February 2023 · City of Chandler, Ordinance No. 5033, 8 December 2022

Bigger than any of these

Next to the world's total, one person's week is tiny. The biggest levers aren't in your chat window:

  • Where data centres are built. The same electricity puts out several times more CO2 on a coal-heavy grid than on a clean one. Try it in 2030.
  • Whether companies publish what they use. The per-question figures here come from a handful of company disclosures and outside estimates, which is why every one of them is a range.
  • Local permits. New data centres need grid connections, water and planning approval, decided in public meetings people can attend.

Claims to read twice

When a company says its AI is green, these are the common ways the wording can say more than the electricity does. They're practices, not accusations: each one is explained by researchers, regulators or reporters.

  • Buying certificates, not clean power

    Renewable-energy certificates are used to calculate "market-based" emissions, the official figures firms report. Researchers estimate that if the trend continues, 42% of committed scope 2 (electricity) emission reductions will not result in real-world mitigation.

    Sources: Nature Climate Change, 9 June 2022 · The Guardian, 15 September 2024

    Read the quotes
    • If this trend continues, 42% of committed scope 2 emission reductions will not result in real-world mitigation.
      Nature Climate Change, 9 June 2022
    • Recs are used to calculate "market-based" emissions, or the official emissions figures used by the firms.
      The Guardian, 15 September 2024

  • Matching over a year, not hour by hour

    A peer-reviewed model found that matching a year's electricity use with clean power has minimal impact on long-run emissions. Matching it hour by hour keeps contributing significantly to cutting them, even as grids get cleaner.

    Sources: Joule, 21 February 2024 (Princeton) · Riepin and Brown, TU Berlin, arXiv 2023

    Read the quotes
    • procurement strategies that match participants' demand with carbon-free generation on an annual basis have minimal impact on long-run system-level CO2 emissions
      Joule, 21 February 2024 (Princeton)
    • Even as grids become cleaner over time, the hourly matching strategy contributes significantly to system-level emissions reduction.
      Riepin and Brown, TU Berlin, arXiv 2023

  • "Carbon neutral" through offsets

    A review estimates that less than 16% of the carbon credits issued to the projects it investigated were real emission reductions. A new EU directive will ban product claims of a neutral, reduced or positive environmental impact based on offsetting.

    Sources: Nature Communications, 14 November 2024 · European Parliament, 17 January 2024

    Read the quotes
    • We estimate that less than 16% of the carbon credits issued to the investigated projects constitute real emission reductions
      Nature Communications, 14 November 2024
    • the directive will ban claims that a product has a neutral, reduced or positive impact on the environment because of emissions offsetting schemes
      European Parliament, 17 January 2024

  • "Water positive"

    One company's water stewardship goal left out the water consumed by the power plants that supply its data centres. And as a former water sustainability manager put it, carbon is a global problem, but water is more localised.

    Sources: Grist, 29 August 2024 · SourceMaterial, 9 April 2025, quoting a former water sustainability manager at a cloud company

    Read the quotes
    • the company's water stewardship goal doesn't include the water consumed by the power plants that supply its data centers
      Grist, 29 August 2024
    • Carbon is a global problem—water is more localised
      SourceMaterial, 9 April 2025, quoting a former water sustainability manager at a cloud company

  • Leaving out the chips and the buildings

    Embodied emissions can exceed 40% of a data centre's total greenhouse gas emissions, so a footprint that leaves them out can miss a large part.

    Source: ICEF Sustainable Data Centers Roadmap, October 2025

    Read the quote
    • embodied emissions can exceed 40% of a data center’s total greenhouse gas emissions and may dominate the lifetime greenhouse gas emissions footprint
      ICEF Sustainable Data Centers Roadmap, October 2025

  • Efficiency, not the total

    Researchers warn that because of rebound effects, efficiency alone won't ensure lower total harm. US data-centre electricity use climbed from 58 TWh in 2014 to 176 TWh in 2023.

    Sources: Luccioni, Strubell and Crawford, arXiv January 2025 · Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 15 January 2025

    Read the quotes
    • Rebound effects undermine the assumption that improved technical efficiency alone will ensure net reductions in environmental harm.
      Luccioni, Strubell and Crawford, arXiv January 2025
    • The total data center electricity usage climbed from 58 TWh in 2014 to 176 TWh in 2023
      Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 15 January 2025
